digests.summary_md: Defense demand is a unifying tailwind today, reflected in surging backlogs at ISSC, OPXS, and CODA and AI-driven government contract wins at SPAI and SATL. Yet that demand backdrop conceals a widening credibility gap for companies that have struggled to convert orders into consistent execution. DFNS, despite benefiting from Iran-conflict urgency, has seen its stock hammered as the market doubts its operational capacity. SIDU’s missile-defense positioning is undermined by heavy dilution and related-party concerns. In firearms, BYRN and RGR face margin compression that sparked sharp re-ratings even as revenue grew. A cluster of pre-revenue space and autonomous flight companies—SPCE, MRLN, XTIA—continues to lean on capital markets, sustaining dilution risk. The batch underscores that strong order books are necessary but far from sufficient to earn investor confidence in this cycle.
